title: US flights resume after "telecommunications outage" causes nationwide ground stop, new tech rollout blamed
html:
US flights have resumed operations after the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) enforced a nationwide ground stop for about four hours.

More than 11,000 US flights were delayed or canceled, causing chaos.

US Secretary of the Department of Transportation, Sean Duffy, said the ground stop order came "following a communication issue impacting all Air Route Traffic Control Centers."

The "telecommunications outage" was blamed on "decades-old analog equipment that simply cannot compete with the demands of the 21st century." He added: "Our routers actually got overloaded with data, and… they started to give us inconsistency in the data from those routers. And because of that, we shut the system down.”

He said that the FAA was set to spend $12.5 billion modernizing the infrastructure, but needed more funds to fully overhaul the system.

However, US Secretary of Homeland Security blamed the outage on this upgrade program. "What it appears to be right now, as Secretary Duffy and the FAA were putting patches into the system, they were putting new equipment and new technology, and that new equipment and new technology was overwhelming the older system. The patchwork doesn't work, we need one complete system."
